{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZgXb0Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDHfkU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 101, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified browser-local ECOM postal-letter journey", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `2761b5778cb2ba6cd9c48a30c2b5ef56c7fe701f`, entering `J ECOM` from MAIN or the index is rejected. `src/navigation.ts` contains no ECOM destination, and ordinary mail represents member or Internet correspondence rather than postal addressing and paper delivery.

This leaves an evidenced service journey unavailable. It is an existing fidelity gap, not a demonstrated regression from the latest FTP merge.

## Expected outcome

Provide this keyboard-operated journey:

`MAIN/index → J ECOM → service guidance → application → one fictional postal recipient and address → original letter → review/edit/cancel → explicit simulated acceptance → inspect receipt → contextual departure`

Historical ECOM arranged printing and physical posting. The application should explain that purpose while performing only a local simulation: no actual postal submission, payment or delivery. One recipient is an intentional demonstration subset, not a claim that historical ECOM supported only one.

Keep the draft and latest receipt in memory for the current ECOM visit. Receipt review must work after acceptance and while visiting guidance; leaving ECOM, disconnecting, reloading, resetting or restoring clears them. No new mailbox, outbox, backup schema or delivery scheduler is required.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction tolerance

Sources researched live on 2026-10-24:

- [Japan Post institutional history, printed p. 349](https://www.japanpost.jp/group/about/milestone/chronicle/pdf/main_4_2_03.pdf) dates submission through approved commercial computer networks to January 31, 1996. This is a readable retrospective institutional account: high confidence in the stated launch date, but it does not name PC-VAN in that passage or specify terminal controls. Its later web services must remain separate.
- [Internet Magazine, April 1996, printed p. 245](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199604-238-news.pdf) has indexed contemporary reporting describing PC-VAN address/letter entry followed by printing and postal delivery. Relevant evidence remains **snippet-only**: the opened PDF extraction omitted that column and page-image retrieval failed. Confidence is moderate for the indexed report.
- [Preserved ECOM material](https://elestamp.o.oo7.jp/Computer_history.htm) remains directly inaccessible with HTTP 403. Indexed text labels a July 6, 1996 log, separates guidance/application/departure, and preserves `J ECOM` in separate March correspondence. These are **snippet-only**, later-preserved observations; they do not supply a complete application transcript. Confidence is moderate, with July-to-November continuity accepted provisionally.
- [Client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html) explicitly lists paid ECOM document posting separately from ordinary mail. The page was readable; release dating remains unresolved, and client features do not authenticate host prompts.
- [Japan Post chronology](https://www.japanpost.jp/corporate/milestone/chronicle/pdf/main_4_2_02.pdf) has indexed text dating seven-digit postcode introduction to February 2, 1998. Direct opening exceeded the tool size limit. This is qualified corroboration for avoiding a mandatory modern postcode format; it does not establish ECOM's original address fields.

The fee evidence conflicts: April reporting quotes 101/106 yen for one/two sheets; indexed July guidance quotes 110/120 yen. Preserve the contradiction without explaining it speculatively. Do not implement a historical price calculator, dispatch timetable or authenticated pagination claim.

**Accepted category D reconstruction:** application field order, validation bounds, editor commands, confirmation, receipt wording/lifetime and contextual returns. Use original Japanese guidance and fictional examples. Exact 1996 application prompts, acceptance identifiers and cancellation controls remain unknown. Do not assign meanings to unverified guidance-list tokens or borrow commands from another service.

### Implementation and existing evidence

Inspect and reuse the relevant patterns in `src/navigation.ts`, `src/connection.ts`, `src/commands.ts`, `src/composer.ts`, `src/main.ts` and `src/terminal.ts`. Composition currently owns terminal input before navigation; `recordsHistory` excludes active drafts, and `invalidate()` clears pending operations. FTP supplies a single-use confirmation precedent. Same-tab restore, cross-tab world replacement and queued commands need explicit ECOM integration.

Prefer a small service-specific owner using existing literal-input/editing patterns. Do not force postal drafts into forum/mail records or introduce a general workflow framework.

Live queries returned no open Issues or PRs. [#3](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/3) records ECOM evidence; [#13](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/13) explicitly separates it from SIG services; [#93](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/93) concerns Internet-addressed mail. None implements this journey.

[PR #100](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/100) and `docs/validation.md` report 360 passing checks with three workers, production FTP journeys and diff review. Those are Coordinator records, not checks performed by this research graph. The earlier default-worker reliability question remains unresolved and is not evidence of an ECOM defect.

Scope excludes actual transport/payment, address lookup, print/PDF generation, multiple recipients, durable postal records, mailbox migration and unrelated historical-service expansion.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Support discoverable `J ECOM` from MAIN and the index without changing existing numbered MAIN mappings. Preserve the guidance/application/departure distinction. Indexed `1`/`2`/`E` menu choices may be used with qualified provenance; additional HELP/BACK/MAIN and receipt controls are explicitly reconstructed. Departure returns to the actual entry parent. ECOM exposes no forum, ordinary-mail, NetNews, OLT, conference or download context.
- [ ] Provide concise original guidance explaining computer-to-paper posting and the local simulation. Supply a clearly fictional recipient/address example usable without real personal information, registration, credentials or payment. Permit anonymous and registered visits. Do not require a seven-digit postcode, resolve an address externally or assert historical address-validation rules.
- [ ] Capture a bounded, nonblank recipient name, postal address and multiline letter. Document product limits as reconstruction. Preserve Japanese, case, indentation, blank lines, full-width/half-width characters and literal markup. Reuse existing explicit text-escape conventions so command-shaped body text can be entered literally. Invalid input retains the current draft and field.
- [ ] Review displays every submitted field and the exact letter. Allow editing all captured values, returning to review, and explicit cancellation. HELP and attempted navigation during a draft must explain how to retain or cancel it; they cannot silently submit or discard it. Empty input, unrelated commands, IME confirmation and leaving a Settings/About dialog cannot approve acceptance.
- [ ] Require explicit approval of the reviewed version. Consume approval before any asynchronous work; repeated or queued approval creates only one receipt. Changes to fields require renewed review. Receipt and success output identify simulated acceptance without claiming postal transmission, charging, delivery or recipient reading. A reconstructed receipt control redisplays the latest accepted fields and letter during the ECOM visit; a later acceptance replaces that receipt.
- [ ] Clear drafts, approval and receipts on service departure, disconnect/reconnect, reload, reset and successful restore/world replacement, including identical-JSON same-tab restore and cross-tab replacement. Stale queued input cannot revive or approve an old application. Settings/About inspection preserves the draft and unsent terminal input unless a world-changing action succeeds.
- [ ] Keep postal fields, body and receipt outside IndexedDB records, durable command history, JSON backups and all resident generation/context paths. Existing in-memory transcript and explicitly exported terminal logs may contain displayed text; document this distinction. Preserve members, forums/posts, ordinary mail/read evidence, conference, OLT, NetNews, consent, settings and empty restored community collections. Normal session/activity bookkeeping may continue. ECOM itself causes no external request, worker/model load, popup or mail-client handoff.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright/controller coverage using current helpers. Include MAIN/index entry and parent returns; contextual command rejection; field bounds; literal Japanese input; review/edit/cancel; repeated approval; receipt inspection and lifetime; Settings/About preservation; reset/restore/cross-tab invalidation; simulated IME protection; and protected-record/history/backup comparisons. Include anonymous restored-empty and registered production keyboard journeys at the existing narrow viewport, with automatic activity paused and AI consent disabled. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, private-context, IME and terminal regression coverage.
- [ ] Update the historical research record, relevant README and Settings/About descriptions, and focused ECOM documentation. Record source dates, access status, confidence, the fee contradiction, provisional late-1996 continuity and all reconstructed controls/limits. Keep routine terminal explanation concise. Copy no archived messages, identities, screenshots or official prose.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test`, using the existing Playwright configuration that includes TypeScript checking and production bundling. The recorded three-worker configuration (`npm test -- --workers=3`) is acceptable; disclose the worker count, failures, corrections and skipped checks accurately. Review the full diff, affected documentation links and `git diff --check`. No new framework, model download, human approval or hardware check is required.

## Optional validation

A newly accessible dated ECOM application transcript may refine field order, commands and receipt presentation. Additional browser-engine or native-IME checks are optional. Recovering exact fees or historical pagination is not a completion gate for this disclosed subset.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable against local production assets before merge.
